text:
Sam (Finance): Heads-up — the March invoice shows a $9,600 negative line (credit) against our GPU spend that Sales says came from a vendor marketplace promotion. It reduced team allocations incorrectly; we need to untangle and decide ledger treatment.
Rina (Sales Ops): Yep that's the marketplace promo I negotiated for Acme customer credits. Vendor applied it directly to the billing account instead of issuing a vendor credit note to the customer. They told me it would be on-account credit, but I didn't expect it to mask internal chargebacks.
Omar (Eng-Infra): Can you paste the invoice line? If the credit is at the billing-account level, our billing export will show "adjustment_type=promo" and null costCenter which breaks attribution.
Sam (Finance): Invoice snippet: "line 452: SKU=GPU_compute, amount=-9600, description='Marketplace promo: ACME_2026Q1'". Export flagged label=unmapped.
Tess (Platform): That means our per-team cost reports lump this into "unassigned" which lowered the ML Platform’s apparent spend. We need to re-run chargebacks so product teams see true usage for budgeting.
VendorBot (cloud-vendor-bot): Automated note: Vendor credit applied: vendor_id=vend-314, external_ref=VEND-ACME-CREDIT-01, amount=9600, applied_at=1769949000.
Rina (Sales Ops): I emailed vendor sales and asked for a vendor invoice/credit memo to route to the customer instead. They responded "investigating" and opened case VEND-3421.
Sam (Finance): Two parallel requests: 1) Accounting: create an internal reverse of the marketplace credit so team-level ledgers reflect consumption (journal entry JRN-2026-03-21-MKT). 2) Ops: work with vendor to reissue as customer-facing credit or reimburse us. Which is faster?
Omar (Eng-Infra): For immediate reporting, we can tag the adjustment in our chargeback pipeline as "manual-marketplace-reclass" and force the $9,600 back to per-team allocations based on tokenized GPU-hour distribution over Mar 1-20. That yields a temporary reallocation CSV for finance.
Tess (Platform): Agree. We'll need the exact distribution factors. Omar, can you generate the GPU-hour histogram for the date range and attach to the ticket?
VendorBot (cloud-vendor-bot): Case created with vendor: VEND-3421. Status: pending_vendor_response.
Rina (Sales Ops): Vendor confirmed they can reissue. ETA 5 business days. They offered a partial refund if we prefer cash over credit.
Sam (Finance): OK — proceed with internal journal (JRN-2026-03-21-MKT) now and mark it as provisional. When vendor resolves, we'll either reverse or finalize. Please document approvals. Approvers: Sam (Finance), Rina (Sales Ops), Tess (Platform).
Omar (Eng-Infra): I'll generate the distribution and upload file: drive.google.com/drive/folders/pm-gpu-chargebacks/marketplace-reclass-2026-03.csv. Also adding an alert to detect marketplace-level credits >$1k that don't have a linked vendor_memo id.
Tess (Platform): Adding a policy: any marketplace credit must include meta label `marketplace_memo` that maps to a vendor invoice. I'll open infra PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-ops/pull/812.
Sam (Finance): Please add the vendor case number and the provisional journal entry to our month-close pack. I'll tag this as "requires follow-up" and won't finalize until vendor case is closed or refund received.
Rina (Sales Ops): Noted. I'll keep chasing VEND-3421 and update here when they commit to refund vs reissue.
VendorBot (cloud-vendor-bot): Update: VEND-3421  vendor_responseETA=72h  offered_refund=false  will_reissue_credit=true
Sam (Finance): Perfect. Thanks everyone. Closing action items: 1) Omar produce distribution CSV, 2) Finance create JRN-2026-03-21-MKT, 3) Rina chase VEND-3421. Post links/ticket numbers once done.
Tess (Platform): Will follow up with a short runbook for marketplace credit handling to avoid this next quarter.
Sam (Finance): Closing thread for now; will reopen if vendor changes stance.
